simple cycles such that every edge belongs to exactly two cycles, counted with multiplicity.

theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

    ∃ C : Multiset (SimpleGraph.Cycle G),
      ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, (C.filter fun c ↦ e ∈ c.edges).card = 2 := by
  sorry

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cycle double cover conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia/Cycle_double_cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/cycle_double_cover_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

The cycle double cover conjecture (Szekeres 1973, Seymour 1979) states that every finite
bridgeless undirected graph has a family of cycles that includes each edge exactly twice.

Here a *cycle* is a connected subgraph all of whose vertices have degree $2$; a single edge
traversed back and forth does not count. A *bridge* is an edge whose removal increases the number
of connected components. Bridgelessness is necessary: a bridge lies on no cycle.

The family is a multiset: some graphs, such as cycle graphs, only have double covers that use the
same cycle twice.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- A multiset `C` of cycles of `G` is a *cycle double cover* of `G` if every edge of `G` lies on
exactly two members of `C`, counted with multiplicity. -/
def IsCycleDoubleCover (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 2

/--
**Cycle double cover conjecture.** Every finite bridgeless graph $G$ has a cycle double cover:
a multiset of cycles of $G$ such that every edge of $G$ belongs to exactly two members of the
multiset, counted with multiplicity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle G), IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  sorry

/-- The empty multiset is a cycle double cover of the edgeless graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_bot_zero : IsCycleDoubleCover (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) 0 := by
  intro e he
  simp at he

/-- The triangle `0 → 1 → 2 → 0` as a cycle of the complete graph on three vertices. -/
def triangleCycle : Cycle (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) where
  base := 0
  walk := .cons (u := 0) (v := 1) (by decide) (.cons (u := 1) (v := 2) (by decide)
    (.cons (u := 2) (v := 0) (by decide) .nil))
  isCycle := by
    rw [Walk.isCycle_def, Walk.isTrail_def]
    exact ⟨by decide, by simp, by decide⟩

/-- The triangle is covered twice by two copies of its only cycle. This shows why the cover is a
multiset rather than a set. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_top_fin_three :
    IsCycleDoubleCover (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) {triangleCycle, triangleCycle} := by
  intro e he
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h a b =>
    simp only [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all <;> decide

/-- A bridge lies on no cycle, so a graph with a bridge has no cycle double cover. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isCycleDoubleCover_of_isBridge {G : SimpleGraph V} {e : Sym2 V} (he : G.IsBridge e)
    (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : ¬ IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  intro hC
  rw [isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem] at he
  have h := hC e he.1
  have hpos : 0 < C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) := by omega
  obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Multiset.countP_pos.mp hpos
  exact he.2 c.walk c.isCycle hc

/-- Bridgelessness is necessary for a cycle double cover to exist, so the hypothesis of
`cycle_double_cover_conjecture` cannot be dropped. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isBridgeless_of_exists_isCycleDoubleCover {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (h : ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle G), IsCycleDoubleCover G C) : G.IsBridgeless := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := h
  intro e _ he
  exact not_isCycleDoubleCover_of_isBridge he C hC

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The cycle double cover conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cycle double cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/cycle_double_cover_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that includes each edge twice.

Here a cycle is a connected subgraph all of whose vertices have degree $2$; a single edge
traversed back and forth does not count. Cycle graphs show that a double cover may have to use
the same cycle twice, so the family is a multiset and edges are counted with multiplicity.
The conjecture is about finite graphs. It is usually stated for multigraphs, but subdividing
every edge preserves bridgelessness and turns any double cover of the subdivision into one of
the original graph, so the simple graph case is equivalent.
-/

namespace CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- `C` is a cycle double cover of `G`: every edge of `G` lies on exactly two members of the
multiset `C` of cycles of `G`, counted with multiplicity. -/
def IsCycleDoubleCover (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Multiset G.Cycle) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, C.countP (e ∈ ·.edges) = 2

/-- **The cycle double cover conjecture.** Every finite bridgeless graph has a family of cycles
that includes each edge exactly twice. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ C : Multiset G.Cycle, IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  sorry

/-- The empty multiset is a cycle double cover exactly of the edgeless graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_zero_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsCycleDoubleCover G 0 ↔ G = ⊥ := by
  simp only [IsCycleDoubleCover, Multiset.countP_zero, OfNat.zero_ne_ofNat, imp_false,
    ← edgeSet_eq_empty, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]

/-- Bridgelessness is necessary: no cycle contains a bridge, so a graph with a cycle double
cover has no bridge. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleDoubleCover.isBridgeless {G : SimpleGraph V} {C : Multiset G.Cycle}
    (hC : IsCycleDoubleCover G C) : G.IsBridgeless := by
  intro e he hb
  obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Multiset.countP_pos.mp (by rw [hC e he]; norm_num)
  exact (isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem.mp hb).2 c.walk c.isCycle hc

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

A *cycle double cover* of a graph $G$ is a multiset of cycles of $G$ such that every edge of $G$
belongs to exactly two members of the multiset, counted with multiplicity. The cycle double cover
conjecture (Szekeres 1973, Seymour 1979) states that every finite bridgeless graph has a cycle
double cover.

The conjecture is usually stated for multigraphs. Subdividing every edge of a multigraph gives a
simple graph with the same bridges, whose cycle double covers correspond to those of the original
multigraph, so the statement for simple graphs is equivalent to the general one.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- A multiset `C` of cycles of `G` is a *cycle double cover* of `G` if every edge of `G` lies on
exactly two members of `C`, counted with multiplicity. A cycle is a closed walk with no repeated
edge and no repeated vertex other than its basepoint, so a single edge traversed back and forth
is not a cycle. Duplicates in `C` are allowed: a cycle graph is double covered only by the
multiset containing its unique cycle twice. -/
def IsCycleDoubleCover (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Multiset G.Cycle) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, C.countP (e ∈ ·.edges) = 2

/-- **Cycle double cover conjecture.** Every finite bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that
includes each edge exactly twice. That is, for every finite bridgeless graph $G$ there is a
multiset of cycles of $G$ such that every edge of $G$ belongs to precisely two of its members,
counted with multiplicity. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ C : Multiset G.Cycle, IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  sorry

/-- The empty multiset is a cycle double cover exactly of the edgeless graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_zero_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsCycleDoubleCover G 0 ↔ G = ⊥ := by
  simp [IsCycleDoubleCover, ← edgeSet_eq_empty, Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]

/-- A bridge lies on no cycle, so a graph with a cycle double cover is bridgeless. This is why the
conjecture only concerns bridgeless graphs. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleDoubleCover.isBridgeless {G : SimpleGraph V} {C : Multiset G.Cycle}
    (hC : IsCycleDoubleCover G C) : G.IsBridgeless := by
  intro e he hb
  have h2 := hC e he
  have hpos : 0 < C.countP (e ∈ ·.edges) := by omega
  obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Multiset.countP_pos.mp hpos
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h v w => exact (isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem.mp hb).2 c.walk c.isCycle hc

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cycle double cover conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cycle double cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/cycle_double_cover_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz73] Szekeres, G., *Polyhedral decompositions of cubic graphs*,
  Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 8 (1973), 367--387.
- [Se79] Seymour, P. D., *Sums of circuits*, in Graph Theory and Related Topics (1979), 341--355.

A *cycle double cover* of a graph is a collection of cycles that together include each edge of
the graph exactly twice. The **cycle double cover conjecture** states that every bridgeless graph
has a cycle double cover.

Here a *cycle* is a connected subgraph all of whose vertices have degree two, so a single edge
traversed back and forth is not a cycle. Cycle graphs and bridgeless cactus graphs only have
double covers that use the same cycle twice, so the collection is a *multiset* of cycles and
edges are counted with multiplicity.

The conjecture is stated for finite simple graphs. This loses no generality: subdividing every
edge of a bridgeless multigraph gives a bridgeless simple graph, and a cycle double cover of the
subdivision contracts to one of the original multigraph.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace CycleDoubleCoverConjecture

variable {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- A multiset `C` of cycles of `G` is a *cycle double cover* of `G` if every edge of `G` lies in
exactly two members of `C`, counted with multiplicity. -/
def IsCycleDoubleCover (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 2

/--
**Cycle double cover conjecture** (Szekeres 1973, Seymour 1979).
Every bridgeless graph has a family of cycles that includes each edge twice.
Precisely: for every finite bridgeless undirected graph $G$ there is a multiset of cycles
of $G$ such that every edge of $G$ belongs to exactly two members of the multiset, counted with
multiplicity.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cycle_double_cover_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle G), IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  sorry

omit [DecidableEq V] in
/-- The graph with no edges is bridgeless. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isBridgeless_bot : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).IsBridgeless := by
  intro e he
  simp at he

/-- The empty multiset is a cycle double cover of the graph with no edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleDoubleCover_bot_zero : IsCycleDoubleCover (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) 0 := by
  intro e he
  simp at he

/-- A cycle double cover of a graph with an edge is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleDoubleCover.ne_zero {G : SimpleGraph V} {C : Multiset (Cycle G)}
    (hC : IsCycleDoubleCover G C) {e : Sym2 V} (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) : C ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  simpa using hC e he

/-- A bridge lies on no cycle, so a graph with a bridge has no cycle double cover. This is why
the conjecture assumes that the graph is bridgeless. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isCycleDoubleCover_of_isBridge {G : SimpleGraph V} {e : Sym2 V} (he : G.IsBridge e)
    (C : Multiset (Cycle G)) : ¬ IsCycleDoubleCover G C := by
  intro hC
  obtain ⟨hmem, hcyc⟩ := isBridge_iff_mem_and_forall_cycle_notMem.mp he
  have h2 := hC e hmem
  have h0 : C.countP (fun c => e ∈ c.edges) = 0 :=
    Multiset.countP_eq_zero.mpr fun c _ => hcyc c.walk c.isCycle
  omega

end CycleDoubleCoverConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (multiset, exactly two, genuine simple cycles, finite simple graphs suffice, edgeless case, ignore the 'proposed solution' section) all match the article and were followed.
modeling_decisions: The list entry says 'includes each edge twice'; following the article ('exactly twice', 'precisely two elements of the multiset') this is formalized as exactly 2, via Multiset.countP = 2.

'Family of cycles' is modeled as a Multiset (Cycle G), as the article explicitly says a multiset is needed (cycle graphs need the same cycle twice). Each Cycle G is a trail, so each member contributes at most 1 to the count of an edge.

Graphs are finite simple graphs (SimpleGraph V with Fintype V), per the decomposition table. The conjecture is usually stated for multigraphs; the simple-graph case is equivalent by subdividing edges (bridgelessness is preserved and covers pull back), as recorded in the module docstring.

SimpleGraph.Cycle bundles a basepoint, so the same geometric cycle has several representatives (rotations/reversals). Counting them as separate members is harmless: it is the same as using a cycle with multiplicity, which the statement permits.

Bridgeless uses the repo's SimpleGraph.IsBridgeless (∀ e ∈ edgeSet, ¬ IsBridge e), where Mathlib's IsBridge means the edge's endpoints become unreachable after deleting it — equivalent to 'removal increases the number of components'. The hypothesis is genuinely restrictive (a bridge blocks any cover; proved as an API lemma).
[DecidableEq V] is assumed so that membership e ∈ c.edges is decidable for countP; this is the same convention as the existing Alon–Tarsi file and does not change the mathematical content.
Edgeless graphs (including empty V) are bridgeless and satisfied by the empty multiset; tested with isBridgeless_bot and isCycleDoubleCover_bot_zero.
The article's 'July 2026 proposed solution' section is ignored; the category is `research open` as recorded in the task status.
